minutes.headline: Sewer Commission voted to send its FY22 budget to the town manager for the Finance Committee review.
minutes.summary: The commission reviewed changes to the FY22 sewer budget since the prior meeting, including a higher Leominster usage estimate and a maintenance-plan commitment from retained earnings. It also discussed the Fitchburg ordinance extension, approved minutes and the annual report, deferred the access-to-counsel policy until full membership, and voted to forward the budget.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to send the FY22 sewer budget, as discussed at the meeting, to the town manager.
The commission accepted the annual report of the sewer commission by vote.
Budget changes since the prior meeting included a higher Leominster usage estimate and a commitment of retained earnings to the maintenance plan.
The commission agreed to ask Fitchburg for an extension on its sewer ordinance review.
The maintenance plan goes at the top of the Feb 23 agenda as a mini workshop, and the access-to-counsel policy waits until the commission has full membership.

why_it_matters: The forwarded budget sets how sewer costs, including Leominster and Fitchburg usage and use of retained earnings, are carried into the FY22 budget that the Finance Committee reviews, which bears on sewer rates paid by ratepayers.
Waived grease trap permit fees and a larger share of retained earnings going to the maintenance plan change how much of the system's upkeep is paid from reserves rather than current revenue.
watch_next: Feb 23 Sewer Commission meeting: the maintenance plan mini workshop is at the top of the agenda.
Fitchburg's response to the request for an extension on the sewer ordinance review, and the Finance Committee review of the FY22 sewer budget.
